- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and prices are falling, model often overcorrects downward; avoid sharp drops; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias.  
- Model frequently overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile; reduce forecast by 1–2% for first 5–7 days.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply 2–4% downward correction.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.1–0.3) and price is trending, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to catch mean reversion.  
- For long-term (15+ day) forecasts, model underestimates mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to align with historical volatility.  
- When sentiment is high and price is near support, model often fails to recognize reversal; add 1–2% downward bias to avoid overbought traps.
